CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted name] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
SPECIMEN: Chorionic villus sample
COLLECTION DATE: [redacted date]
REPORT DATE: [redacted date]
ACCESSION: [redacted ID]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal testing requested for advanced maternal age (37 years). Ultrasound gestational age: 13 weeks.

TEST PERFORMED
G-banded chromosome analysis of cultured chorionic villi

RESULT
Karyotype: 46,XY

Normal male chromosome complement

INTERPRETATION
G-banded analysis reveals a normal male karyotype with no evidence of trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) or other numerical or major structural chromosomal abnormalities. Twenty metaphases were analyzed at a resolution of 400-450 bands.

This analysis is sufficient for detection of numerical abnormalities and major structural rearrangements but may not detect subtle structural abnormalities, low-level mosaicism (<10%), or submicroscopic deletions/duplications.

This report supersedes the preliminary rapid aneuploidy screening (QF-PCR) performed one week prior.

METHODOLOGY
Chorionic villus tissue was cultured according to standard protocols. Chromosome analysis was performed using G-banding technique on cultured cells. Analysis included examination of 20 metaphase cells and karyotyping of 5 cells.

LIMITATIONS
- Cannot detect balanced rearrangements that do not result in gain or loss of chromosomal material
- Mosaicism below 10% may not be detected
- Submicroscopic abnormalities require molecular cytogenetic techniques for detection
- Maternal cell contamination, while unlikely, cannot be completely excluded

RECOMMENDATIONS
No additional cytogenetic testing indicated based on these results. Routine prenatal care should continue. Genetic counseling is available if desired.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD

This laboratory is accredited by CAP (#[redacted ID]) and CLIA certified (#[redacted ID])
